newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end sharply higher.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended sharply higher on Thursday, led by platinum group metals and silver, traders said.
In buoyant trade, most silver, platinum and palladium futures, which had hit their daily limits from the outset, held onto early gains for most of the day.

Benchmark December silver rocketed by its six yen per 10 grams limit at 200.2 yen, while benchmark December platinum hit the 50 yen limit at 1,432 yen at the close. Benchmark December palladium jumped by the 22 yen limit to 565 yen.
A widespread perception that the dollar will stay strong against the yen helped boost market sentiment of yen-based precious metal futures, the traders said.
Activity in platinum was the most active, as views that platinum has lagged behind gains in silver and palladium attracted interest in the metal.

Gold tracked gains in other metals, although gains were limited as they were unsure whether spot gold has found a floor for the near-term. Gold prices ranged from 20 yen to 31 yen per gram firmer, with most-active benchmark December finishing up 26 yen at 1,363 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $343.50/80 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $342.80/343.30 in New York.

A widening gold/platinum spread prompted individual investors to sell platinum after buying gold earlier in the day. But investors who were taking profits in platinum, turned buyers later in the day, traders said.

Palladium continued to benefit from the deadlocked Japan-Russia platinum group metal talks. "As long as there is no hint as to when the talks will be held, palladium prices will be firmer in the speculative move. Once the timing of the talks is finalised, prices could tumble," one trader said.
